name: backpressure-streaming-p4
prompt: how do I keep a fast producer from overwhelming a slow consumer when streaming records through a pipeline

chunks.content: decided to give the pipeline a bounded buffer so when the slow consumer falls behind the channel fills and the fast producer blocks on send, naturally pacing itself to the consumer's rate
the network layer uses a credit window: the receiver advertises how many records it has room for and the sender stops once credits run out until more are granted
switched to a pull-based reactive stream where the consumer signals demand for n items and the producer only emits up to what was requested, so it can never get ahead of what the consumer can handle
for the non-critical metrics stream we instead drop the oldest buffered samples when full, trading completeness for keeping the producer unblocked
the health-tracker screen plots the user's blood pressure readings over the last month with a slow upward trend line
the daily digest is compiled at 6am in the recipient's timezone
transient success messages now appear as a toast that fades after three seconds
read-only analytics queries are routed to the standby replica
marketing sends are throttled to 500 messages a minute to stay under the provider's rate cap
the new onboarding tour is behind a flag for a staged rollout
fixed plural rules for languages with more than two plural forms
refresh tokens rotate on every use and the old one is revoked
the facilities ticket about pressure-washing the loading dock was closed after the contractor finished
boosted exact title matches above body matches in the search ranking
